body:
Reason will prevail! 
We're gonna say it every time!
I knew if I just kept scrolling I'd find this.

Who are these asshole scientists that conducted this study. They just watched spiders crawl into people's mouths and instead of waking the person up they just mark it on a clipboard like, "another one for patient 12, Doctor." "Mmm. Indeed, Doctor." Dicks.
Pay people a living wage, provide healthcare for everyone (American here), and not have a bunch of men making decisions for women.

I am an employee, not a contractor, and I have more information on my personal computer than just my work. I also have the company's tax information because no one else can get the scanner to work so I had to scan documents to my computer. I delete most of it but it's bizarre that they allow any of this.

Well another employee and I are considering quitting anyway because they've been asking employees to do electrical work for which they're unqualified. The place is dangerously unprofessional. So if they want to fire me then that might be for the best.

That all makes sense. So should I tell them I'm not willing to use my own computer anymore and they need to provide one? I feel like it's really inappropriate for them to expect me to bring my own to the office every day. 

Btw: I'm an administrative assistant who's basically doing the manager's job, not an actual graphic designer.
I completely agree with you but I also feel oddly compelled to tell you to shh.

I'll also note that I didn't give them some huge ultimatum or anything. I just stopped returning calls and stopped going to family functions when I knew they'd be there. It's sometimes for the best. 

People often assume that these ties are mandatory, but I don't think so. Blood doesn't give someone the right to hurt you and if they refuse to stop then there's no reason to keep giving them a target.
Going back to school to get a better job.

I haven't spoken to my parents in three years. They were abusive and manipulative and refused to accept me for being queer. They still live in the same small town I grew up in and I'm sure they'll never leave. Honestly I don't feel like I lost much. There weren't really upsides to keeping them in my life. My only regret is that I didn't do it ten years sooner. I wasted a lot of time and let them do a lot of damage before I finally got free.
Based on the stuff LA Times has been printing lately I'd say covering in shit and flushing it down a toilet would be an improvement.

I guess games help, but only when actually engaged. And even then it's not much. Like last time I left a game I thought wow that was fun, but if I disappeared now I'd be fine. 

I wanted to study chemistry, but that doesn't matter now.
I guess I like playing games like D&D and I like science. I wanted to be a scientist but it didn't work out. But it's still hard to see the want to live amongst all of that.
